key_insight: A high-fidelity transonic-wing dataset couples aerodynamic and structural responses to benchmark machine learning for multidisciplinary wing design.
engineering_relevance: The dataset supports ML surrogates that could accelerate wing design while accounting for aerodynamic performance and structural integrity.
method: Parameterize wing planforms and airfoil sections using geometric variables and class-shape transformation.
Vary Mach number, angle of attack, altitude, and structural load factor in static aerostructural analyses.
Train ML models to predict aerodynamic surface quantities, integrated performance, and wingbox failure distributions.
evidence_signal: The dataset contains 2,471 samples plus three out-of-distribution samples; reported ML prediction NRMSE is at most 0.0309 for aerodynamic quantities and 0.1189 for wingbox failure distributions.
watch_item: Coverage is limited to static cruise aerostructural behavior, and three out-of-distribution samples provide limited evidence of broader generalization.
paper_title: High-Fidelity Aerostructural Dataset of Transonic Wings in Cruise Conditions
